what_it_does: When engineers want to find the best version of a chip design — the sweet spot between speed, power, and area — they explore a large space of possible configurations. Most tools treat a design as a flat list of numbers (parameter values) and search that space blindly, ignoring the fact that real chip designs have a hierarchical tree structure: a system-on-chip contains processors, which contain functional units, which contain sub-blocks. This paper proposes a similarity measure (called a kernel) that compares two designs based on their tree structures rather than just their parameter values, so that designs with similar architectural shapes are recognized as more alike. Importance weights derived from how much each module contributes to the final circuit metrics are folded in, and clustering based on this tree kernel helps direct where to run the expensive synthesis (turning a blueprint into actual circuit area-and-timing numbers).
